title: engram_root_recovery_live.rs restarted states recover on an undeclared Real budget clock
outcome: src/tests/engram_root_recovery_live.rs builds restarted AppStates with AppState::new_with_paths_and_engram_transport_for_test (about lines 998 and 1111 at 62ffe92). Its constructor runs eager boot recovery inline, so those states read the Engram budget clock (the boot budget and per-operation deadlines) on the default, undeclared Real clock. No test chose a clock first. Slice 1's AppState::new_with_paths_engram_transport_and_clock_for_test chooses the clock before the boot's own recovery. engram_boot_recovery_targets.rs, engram_uncertain_begin.rs and the B3 restart tests already use it. These two sites are outside every batch region of the budget-clock decomposition. The final batch's undeclared-Real rejection would therefore fail them.
acceptance: Each restarted AppState in src/tests/engram_root_recovery_live.rs chooses its Engram budget clock before its boot recovery reads it, through new_with_paths_engram_transport_and_clock_for_test: the shared scripted clock, or EngramBudgetClock::Real with its reason in a comment. Any budget-expiry assertion there either advances the same scripted clock across the causal boundary with an unadvanced positive control, or declares Real.
No production change, and no expectation in that file is weakened.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree; its run directory and fingerprint are cited in a note.

A pinned live launcher run, `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs live --engram-binary <absolute path> --engram-sha256 <sha256>`, run as one call in the named root, passes on the exact reviewed tree. Its engram-live stage log shows live_root_restart_after_lost_evaluate_replays_issued_grant_without_rebinding and live_root_restart_after_lost_begin_never_blindly_redelivers passing among the root_recovery_live tests. Its run directory, the binary path and the sha256 are cited in a note.
